geo.title: Get started

Recreate Eratosthenes with a stick, a shadow, and two cities.

Goal: I can name and measure angles and describe how Eratosthenes used them.

slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
An angle is two rays with a common endpoint, the vertex. We name it with three points, vertex in the middle, like angle ABC, and measure it in degrees.

Around 240 BCE, Eratosthenes noticed that at noon on one day the Sun was straight overhead at Syene, while at Alexandria a vertical stick cast a shadow at about 7.2 degrees. The Sun's rays are nearly parallel, so the angle at Earth's center between the two cities is also about 7.2 degrees, which is 1/50 of 360 degrees. So Earth's circumference is about 50 times the distance between the cities.

slides.title: Check yourself
slides.html: If two cities are 800 km apart and the angle is 7.2 degrees, about how big is Earth's circumference?
slides.reveal: 7.2 degrees is 1/50 of 360 degrees, so about 50 times 800 km = 40,000 km.
